title: Basic variables
description:
## Vars
If you come from other languages, you probably think of variables as mutable little bundles of data. Not in Haskell. In Haskell, bindings are immutable. Advanced features can simulate mutation, but most of the time you don't need them. To create a variable in Haskell in a function (a do block), you use:
```haskell
let <varName> = <value>
```
Outside a `do` block, you don't need the `let`.
_Notice the first letter must be a lowercase letter_. Pretty simple!
## String concatenation.
You concatenate strings in Haskell with the `++` operator.
```haskell
putStrLn ("Hello, " ++ "World!")
```
Notice the () around the ++ in the previous line: Parentheses are needed because we want to concatenate the strings first before passing the final result to putStrLn
